cards.info: What is the definition of an angle of elevation?
cards.backInfo: The angle formed between a horizontal line and the line of sight looking up at an object.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A right triangle where the base is labeled 'Horizontal Distance (Adjacent)', the vertical side is 'Height (Opposite)', and the angle at the base is 'Angle of Elevation'.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/674ad56e-2121-4d6e-9249-fed3b0638708-1786505984620-81.webp)

cards.info: What is the definition of an angle of depression?
cards.backInfo: The angle formed between a horizontal line and the line of sight looking down at an object.

cards.info: Which triangle leg represents the horizontal distance from an observer?
cards.backInfo: The horizontal distance represents the adjacent leg of the right triangle.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A right triangle where the base is labeled 'Horizontal Distance (Adjacent)', the vertical side is 'Height (Opposite)', and the angle at the base is 'Angle of Elevation'.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/674ad56e-2121-4d6e-9249-fed3b0638708-1786505984620-81.webp)

cards.info: Which triangle leg represents the vertical height of an object?
cards.backInfo: The vertical height represents the opposite leg of the right triangle.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A right triangle where the base is labeled 'Horizontal Distance (Adjacent)', the vertical side is 'Height (Opposite)', and the angle at the base is 'Angle of Elevation'.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/674ad56e-2121-4d6e-9249-fed3b0638708-1786505984620-81.webp)

cards.info: What is the tangent ratio formula for right triangles?
cards.backInfo: The formula is $\tan(\theta) = \text{opposite} / \text{adjacent}$.

cards.info: How do you calculate height using horizontal distance and angle?
cards.backInfo: Multiply the horizontal distance by the tangent of the angle: $\text{Height} = \text{Distance} \times \tan(\theta)$.

cards.info: How does an angle of elevation compare to an angle of depression?
cards.backInfo: The angle of elevation from Point A to B equals the angle of depression from B to A.

cards.info: Why is using the sine ratio often a mistake in these problems?
cards.backInfo: Sine requires the hypotenuse, but these problems usually provide only the horizontal distance (adjacent) and height (opposite).

cards.info: From what line must an angle of depression always be measured?
cards.backInfo: It must be measured from a horizontal line of sight, not from a vertical line like a wall.

cards.info: How do you calculate horizontal distance using height and angle?
cards.backInfo: Divide the vertical height by the tangent of the angle: $\text{Distance} = \text{Height} / \tan(\theta)$.

cards.info: In a sketch, where is the angle of elevation located?
cards.backInfo: It is located at the observer's eye level, between the horizontal ground and the upward line of sight.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A right triangle where the base is labeled 'Horizontal Distance (Adjacent)', the vertical side is 'Height (Opposite)', and the angle at the base is 'Angle of Elevation'.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/674ad56e-2121-4d6e-9249-fed3b0638708-1786505984620-81.webp)

cards.info: Does an angle of depression look above or below the horizontal?
cards.backInfo: It looks below the horizontal line of sight down toward an object.

cards.info: When modeling a building's shadow, what triangle part is the shadow?
cards.backInfo: The shadow on the ground represents the horizontal distance or the adjacent leg.

cards.info: In a right triangle model, what represents the 'opposite' leg?
cards.backInfo: The vertical height of the object being observed represents the opposite leg.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A right triangle where the base is labeled 'Horizontal Distance (Adjacent)', the vertical side is 'Height (Opposite)', and the angle at the base is 'Angle of Elevation'.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/674ad56e-2121-4d6e-9249-fed3b0638708-1786505984620-81.webp)

cards.info: Which trigonometric ratio relates vertical height to horizontal distance?
cards.backInfo: The tangent ratio: $\tan(\theta) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$.

cards.info: Solve for $h$: A 50ft distance and $30^\circ$ angle of elevation.
cards.backInfo: $h = 50 \times \tan(30^\circ)$.

cards.info: Why are angles of elevation and depression between two points equal?
cards.backInfo: They are equal because they function as alternate interior angles between two parallel horizontal lines.

cards.info: When should you avoid using the cosine ratio in these problems?
cards.backInfo: Avoid cosine when the hypotenuse (direct line of sight distance) is neither given nor required.

cards.info: What is the error in measuring depression from a vertical wall?
cards.backInfo: The angle must be measured from the horizontal; measuring from the wall uses the wrong reference axis.

cards.info: If height exceeds horizontal distance, what is true of the angle?
cards.backInfo: The angle of elevation will be greater than $45^\circ$ because $\tan(\theta) > 1$.
